miniProject.title: Mutable-priority heap, a derived boundary and a room scheduler
miniProject.brief: Build an indexed heap with update and remove, derive one binary-search-on-the-answer boundary from its predicate before running examples, and solve an unseen tree problem and a two-heap scheduling problem with adversarial tests and a worst-case defense.
steps: Implement an indexed min-heap with push, pop, peek, update(item, priority) and remove(item), backed by a position map. Write both invariants (heap order on the array, and pos[item] equals the item's index) and the cost of each operation.

Test it with a Hypothesis rule-based state machine against a dict oracle that answers the minimum by scanning, checking both invariants after every step. Seed one defect, such as an update that only sifts down or a swap that forgets the position map, and keep the shrunk history.

Solve LC 1011 Capacity To Ship Packages Within D Days without reading its tags. Write the predicate feasible(c), prove it monotone, set lo = max(weights) and hi = sum(weights), and derive the loop condition and updates from the invariant (feasible(hi) holds, everything below lo fails) before running any example. The examples answer 15, 6 and 3.

Solve LC 236 Lowest Common Ancestor of a Binary Tree recursively, then defend the worst case: a path-shaped tree of \(10^5\) nodes exceeds CPython's default recursion limit of 1000, so add an iterative version with a parent map and test both against an ancestor-set oracle on random trees.

Solve LC 2402 Meeting Rooms III with two heaps, free rooms by number and busy rooms by end time and number. Write adversarial tests for chained delays, equal end times and a meeting that starts exactly when a room frees, and compare against a brute-force simulator on small random inputs. The examples answer 0 and 1.

Write the worst-case notes: the \(O(m \log m + m \log n)\) bound for LC 2402, and why delayed end times can reach about \(5 \times 10^{10}\) with one room, which overflows 32-bit integers in a fixed-width language.
deliverables: The indexed heap module with invariants, cost notes, the state machine and the seeded-defect history.
The LC 1011 boundary derivation, written before code, with the monotonicity proof.
LC 236 and LC 2402 solutions with adversarial and differential tests and the worst-case notes.

checks.name: LeetCode 1011: Capacity To Ship Packages Within D Days
checks.note: Submit once; the derivation should make the first submission pass.

checks.name: LeetCode 236: Lowest Common Ancestor of a Binary Tree

rubric.pass: The state machine passes with both invariants checked after every step, and the seeded defect fails with a shrunk history.
rubric.strong: Update and remove are tested on the root and the last slot, and swap counts on random histories stay within the stated logarithmic bounds.

rubric.pass: The invariant and updates are written before any example runs, and all three examples pass on the first run.
rubric.strong: A property test checks that the answer is the smallest feasible capacity: feasible(answer) holds and feasible(answer - 1) fails.

rubric.pass: Both versions agree with the oracle, and the iterative version handles the \(10^5\)-node path.
rubric.strong: The write-up shows the recursive failure on the deep tree and states the \(O(h)\) space of each version.

rubric.pass: LC 2402 is accepted, and the brute-force simulator agrees on random small inputs with ties and back-to-back meetings.
rubric.strong: The tie rules are stated as invariants of the two heaps, and the overflow note names the largest end time the constraints allow.

miniProject.feedsInto: Capstone correctness library: the mutable-priority heap. Failure evidence: its seeded defect. The room scheduler is a first scheduler artifact for the milestone.
